newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end softer as early gains melt away.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end softer as early gains melt away.

text.p: Gains racked up on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in Friday's morning session melted away by the end of the day as profit-taking and position squaring weighed on the market in the afternoon, brokers said.
Buying linked to the futures market also petered out, weakening stock indices in the cash market, they said.

The cash benchmark Nikkei 225 average settled 15.18 points or 0.07 percent lower at 21,020.36, after swinging as high as 21,155.22. In the futures market, the key December futures were down 20 points at 21,100.
"Foreign investors who had been buying recently and leading the market were quiet due to the Thanksgiving holiday, but in spite of that, losses were not that heavy," one broker said.
overwhelmed winners 670 issues to 411, while 160 issues were unchanged. Turnover was 292 million shares, down from the trade of 316 million on Thursday.
In the morning session, hopes that investment trusts

launching new trust funds would buy lifted the index, but the buoyant state did not last long. However, after a sharp fall of more than 300 points on Thursday, some investors were ready to buy again, preventing a plunge. "Bargain hunters were fairly active and some global issues such as Honda Motor Corp were sought after," said Harushige Kobayashi, Yamaichi Securities deputy general manager.
"But many other stocks slumped to record lows again, watering down the gains," Kobayashi added.
Market sources said the Nikkei average's habitat was likely

to be a range from 20,500 to 21,500 in the near term. "The floor is firming, as interest rates are not likely to be raised soon and pension funds are eager to buy on dips," said Haruo Nakaharu, strategist at Toyo Securities.
"But unless the index can keep its head up above the end-March level of 21,406, it may not have the strength to break out of that box," he added.

Brokers added that with the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey on business sentiment out, the upcoming expiry of the December Nikkei 225 futures and options, called the special quotations (SQ), was the next item of interest.

"It depends on how smoothly the rollover goes but the market will be sensitive next week to arbitrage-linked trade and futures positions," a "Big Four" brokerage broker said. In other indices, the broader TOPIX lost 5.58 points or 0.36 percent to 1,562.80. The Nikkei 300 was down 1.01 points or 0.34 percent at 295.56. The second section index fell 10.29 points or 0.52 percent to 1,957.15.

Second section turnover was 11.04 million shares, not much different from the 11.8 million traded on Thursday. The over-the counter-index stood at 1,396.18, down 4.48 points or 0.32 percent, in late Tokyo trade.

Honda Motor Co Ltd was the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse, with volume totalling 5.06 million shares. It settled unchanged from Thursday's 3,360 yen after climbing by as much as 60 yen. Second-seeded Hitachi Ltd added 10 to close at
1,060 yen on 4.56 million shares.
Yaohan Japan Corp was at the list of top percentage losers, after falling 100 yen to land at a record low of 500 yen.
"Our share prices fell on rumours that we have no specific measures to cope with the redemption of a 11.7 billion yen warrant, but arrangements have been made to finance it," a Yaohan spokesman said.
Construction firms were mostly lower, with Shimizu Corp down 14 yen at 950. Obayashi Corp lost 10 to 855 yen.

On a sector basis, gas, pulp/paper, machinery, miscellaneous manufacturers, insurance and communications led the pack of gainers. Iron/steel, fisheries, railway/bus, mining and land transport were the main retreaters. -- Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
